alerts.title: Uncontrolled hypothyroidism with missed levothyroxine doses
alerts.message: Patient on levothyroxine 50 mcg has TSH 12.4 mIU/L (target below 4.5) with low free T4, and reports frequently forgetting the thyroid tablet. Weight gain, fatigue, cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin, periorbital puffiness and delayed ankle reflex relaxation are consistent with under-replacement. The clinician plan continues levothyroxine unchanged without addressing adherence or dose adjustment. Weight gain is also not established as caused by DTG, and hypothyroidism is a plausible non-drug explanation for the 9 kg gain.

evidence.recommended_action: Address levothyroxine adherence and review the dose given the elevated TSH and low free T4 before attributing the weight gain to DTG; consider the thyroid disorder as the primary cause.

alerts.title: Proposed DTG switch for weight gain lacks guideline support
alerts.message: Guidance states the association of DTG with weight gain is not considered causal and may reflect comparatively lower metabolic toxicity than older regimens. Patient BMI is 33 with untreated or undertreated hypothyroidism, a recognised cause of weight gain. Switching from DTG for weight gain alone would not be guideline-supported while thyroid status is uncorrected, and would risk losing an effective regimen with suppressed viral load (<50 copies/mL).

evidence.recommended_action: Do not switch from DTG for weight gain until thyroid replacement is optimised and re-assessed; continue viral load monitoring every 6 months per guideline.

alerts.title: Abnormal weight gain on DTG should be reported as adverse effect
alerts.message: Guidance lists abnormal weight gain as an adverse effect associated with DTG that should be recorded on the adverse event reporting form. Patient has documented weight gain of about 9 kg over the past year. The record does not show this was reported, and the clinician plan does not document an adverse event assessment.

evidence.recommended_action: Document the weight gain as a possible adverse effect of DTG on the adverse event form, alongside the thyroid findings as a competing cause.

alerts.title: Hyperglycaemia risk screening incomplete at BMI 33
alerts.message: Guidance recommends hyperglycaemia screening for patients transitioning to DTG who have two or more risk factors, including BMI of 25 or above, age 30 or above and hypertension history. Patient has BMI 33, age 45 and BP 128/82. Fasting glucose today is 5.6 mmol/L, but the plan does not document a formal risk-factor screening decision or follow-up glucose plan.

evidence.recommended_action: Complete the hyperglycaemia risk-factor assessment per the DTG flowchart and document the decision on repeat glucose testing given fasting glucose 5.6 mmol/L and BMI 33.
